svg.text: Bench bill of materials
Every physical object the session needs. Tick it, then start.
NOTHING HERE NEEDS ACQUIRING. Every item was confirmed on hand on 2026-09-11, the 830-point breadboard included. This box exists so that anything
a later revision adds lands on page 1 rather than being discovered on page 13.
TMC2209 StepStick (FYSETC)
1 of 6
The driver. Headers arrived PRE-SOLDERED, confirmed by
opening the box, so page 5 is a skip. All six are one
revision, so one Vref carries to all five later.
ESP32-C5-DevKitC-1
Already on the bench. It stays OFF the breadboard - page
8 says why - so every wire that reaches it is
male-to-female.
NEMA 17 + printed stand-in axle
The load. The axle is PLA, which is why every commanded
speed is REFUSED above this image's cap. The cap is
compiled in and can only be lowered at build time, never
raised and never from a console.
Breadboard, full-size 830-point
63 rows, two rail pairs, an 0.3 in centre channel. The
channel is the only reason a StepStick works on a
breadboard at all - page 8.
Jumper wires, male-to-FEMALE
Three signals (STEP, DIR, EN), the two rail feeds, and
the Hall's 3 flying leads. Female onto the ESP32's pins,
male into the board.
Jumper wires, male-to-male
Board-internal: VIO, GND (logic), MS1 and MS2 to the
rails, plus 2 RAIL LINKS: the two rail pairs are
separate nodes and both are in use. Counts derive from
the parsed table.
JST-XH 4-way mating pigtail
THE MOTOR PLUG CANNOT ENTER A BREADBOARD. The pigtail's
four flying leads can. Page 2 shows exactly where they
terminate.
100 uF electrolytic, 35 V or more
The bulk capacitor. Its legs need trimming and bending
before it will reach the right two holes - lead prep on
page 2.
Hookup wire, 22 AWG SOLID core
30 cm
Red and black, PSU terminal to the board. Solid, not
stranded: stranded frays in a breadboard hole, will not
hold, and leave a strand behind.
Flat screwdriver, 2 mm blade
The Vref trimpot on page 27, and the PSU's terminals. A
blade that does not fit the pot slips off it onto a pad.
Multimeter with a continuity beep
Coil pairs (page 9), continuity (page 26), Vref (page
27). Continuity and DC volts on a 2 V range are all it
needs.
USB-C cable, PC to ESP32
Console and logic power. A DATA cable - a charge-only
lead gives a board that looks alive and never appears as
a serial port.
Bench PSU, current-limited
VM, and the most useful safety device on the bench. 9 V
at a 0.5 A LIMIT for first power, 20 V for the soak. A
wiring fault trips the limit, not the driver.
RotoPD USB-C trigger -- NOT USED
struck
I2C-configured and DEFAULTS TO 5 V, so it cannot be
trusted to come up at the voltage you set, and it
current-limits nothing. Struck, not deleted, so it is
not bought again.
Hex key for the drum set screw
Fit the stand-in drum, and MARK it - a tape flag will do
- so that `step 0 3200` is a readable result rather than
a guess.
Heatsink (supplied, loose)
not used
Deliberately not installed. Page 2 has the reasoning and
the one condition that would change it.
A1121LUA-T Hall sensor
NEW THIS SESSION - gate 3 had none. 3-pin SIP, not
TO-92. Page 23 says which way round it goes; the centre
lead is GND whichever way you read it.
Magnet, O6x3 N42, in the disc
fitted
You are not prising it out to look at it. Page 25 reads
its outward face with a SPARE magnet instead: repel =
south = correct.
Spare magnet, same batch
The polarity meter. It identifies its own south face
against the sensor, and then reads the glued one without
touching it. Page 25.
Resistor, 10 kohm, any type
The Hall's pull-up, OUT to 3V3. The output is OPEN
DRAIN: it can pull the pin down and cannot pull it up,
so without this `hall` reads noise.
Ceramic capacitor, 0.1 uF
Across the sensor's VCC and GND, at the sensor end. The
datasheet states it in words and the flying leads are
long.
